<description>
This adds a test that passes on master and fails with the diff from #34618 applied, as davidgumberg asked in #34722. It covers both things that diff removes for a compact block more than two blocks ahead of the tip.

If the node already requested the block from this peer, it sends another `getdata` for the full block. Without that `getdata`, the block stays in flight from this peer and nothing requests it again until the block download timeout disconnects the peer. This check is the one shuv-amp proposed in #34722.

Otherwise, from a high-bandwidth peer, the node handles the header as a headers message (`fRevertToHeaderProcessing`). Most of that work is done anyway. As 151henry151 pointed out in #34618, one part is not: protecting an outbound peer from eviction (`m_chain_sync.m_protect`). The test checks for the "Protecting outbound peer" debug log line.

Each check fails when only its branch is disabled: `fRevertToHeaderProcessing = false` fails the protection check, and `if (false)` in place of `if (requested_block_from_this_peer)` makes the `getdata` check time out. shuv-amp first tested the two branches separately in #34618.

Fixes #34618.

*Made with my usual tools: a computer, the Internet and an LLM. The mistakes, as usual, are all mine.*
</description>

crACK de16833975f3ec98dc96120e9b6e905709453aec

Nicely closes the gap from #34618 — both uncovered sub-branches of the "more than two blocks ahead of the tip" path are exercised:

- `test_requested` → the `requested_block_from_this_peer` branch: the still-in-flight block triggers the `GETDATA MSG_BLOCK` re-request, caught by `wait_for_getdata([blocks[-1].hash_int])`. Deleting that branch makes the re-request vanish and the wait time out.
- `test_unrequested_from_hb_peer` → the `fRevertToHeaderProcessing = true` → `ProcessHeadersMessage(…, via_compact_block=true)` branch. I traced the asserted log: `Protecting outbound peer=%d from eviction` is emitted only inside `ProcessHeadersMessage` (net_processing.cpp:3209, under `IsFullOutboundConn()`), and for this compact-block message that function is reachable only via `fRevertToHeaderProcessing`. The inbound peer's `msg_headers(blocks[:2])` can't produce it (not an outbound conn), and the earlier full `msg_block` doesn't pass through `ProcessHeadersMessage`, so `m_chain_sync.m_protect` is still false when the cmpctblock arrives — the log is a genuine regression signal for this branch.

Non-blocking suggestion: the header path is asserted indirectly via the eviction-protection log, so a future refactor that moves that logic could let the test keep passing while silently no longer covering `fRevertToHeaderProcessing`. Additionally asserting the header was accepted (e.g. it appears as a headers-only tip in `getchaintips`) would make the coverage robust to that.

Code-review only — didn't build/run locally.
</new_statements>
